# Set up

Input from `01_metat-analysis-eukrhythmic.qmd` and from curated heterotrophy transcript profiling work in `heterotrophy-euk-focused`. This document (1) curates the taxonomy and writes the handoff table `data/processed/long_frenemies_annot_tax.RData` (read by 03 and 04 through `load_long_annot()`), (2) runs the taxonomic grain ladder that fixes the analysis grain at rank 4, then (3) saves the rank-4 paired table `data/processed/paired_L4.RData` that 04–07 read through `load_paired()`.

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
source(if (file.exists("_setup.R")) "_setup.R" else "scripts/_setup.R")  
# locator: works from project root (render) or scripts/ (interactive)

# TRUE rewrites the ~420 MB handoff RData. Leave FALSE unless the curation
# below changed; later scripts read the copy on disk.
WRITE_HANDOFF <- FALSE
```

```{r load data}
load("data/processed/frenemies-longdfs-gr-mcr.RData", verbose = TRUE)
```

```{r}
glimpse(long_frenemies_annot)
head(long_frenemies_annot)
```

# Taxonomic curation

The column `SUPERGROUP_18S` is close to the 18S rRNA gene tag-sequencing results to help us draw conclusions regarding the comparison. This curation is helpful for later comparison to 18S rRNA gene amplicon work, but we also need to perform manual curation. Pair taxonomic classification with full_classification. Below generates `long_frenemies_annot_tax`.

Manual curation
```{r manual curation of taxa}
myzozoa <- c("Perkinsea", "Chromerida", "Colpodellida", "Colponemidia", "Apicomplexa", "Squirmida") # at phylum
class_gyrista <- c("Bacillariophyceae","Bolidophyceae","Chrysophyceae", "Dictyochophyceae", "Eustigmatophyceae", "Ochromonadales","Pelagophyceae", "Xanthophyceae")
class_bigyra <- c("Opalozoa", "Labyrinthulomycetes")

long_frenemies_annot_tax <- long_frenemies_annot %>% 
  filter(Domain == "Eukaryota") %>% 
  # Alveolata
  mutate(SUPERGROUP_PHYLUM = case_when(
    (is.na(Supergroup)) ~ "Eukaryote-Unannotated",
    (grepl("_X", Phylum) | is.na(Phylum)) ~ paste(Supergroup, "Unannotated", sep = "-"),
    # Alveolata
    (Supergroup == "Alveolata" & (is.na(Phylum) | Phylum == "Alveolata_X")) ~ "Alveolata-Unannotated",
    (Supergroup == "Alveolata" & Order == "Syndiniales") ~ "Alveolata-Syndiniales",
    Phylum %in% myzozoa ~ "Alveolata-Myzozoa",
    # Green algae
    Supergroup == "Rhodelphea" ~ "Archaeplastida-Rhodelphea",
    #Stramenopiles (Obiol et al. 2024 - https://academic.oup.com/femsec/article/100/11/fiae130/7815208)
    Class %in% class_gyrista ~ "Stramenopiles-Gyrista",
    Class %in% class_bigyra ~ "Stramenopiles-Bigyra",
    Phylum == "Synurophyceae" ~ "Stramenopiles-Gyrista",
    Phylum == "Oomycota" ~ "Stramenopiles-Gyrista",
    Phylum == "Marine_stramenopiles_MASTs group" ~ "Stramenopiles-Bigyra",
    Supergroup == "Eukaryota incertae sedis" ~ Phylum,
    Supergroup == "Haptista" ~ paste("Hacrobia", Phylum, sep = "-"),
    #
    Phylum == "Choanoflagellida" ~ "Opisthokonta-Choanoflagellata",
    #
    TRUE ~ paste(Supergroup, Phylum, sep = "-"))) %>%
  ### Continued
  mutate(SUPERGROUP_0 = case_when(
    grepl("Alveolata-", SUPERGROUP_PHYLUM) ~ SUPERGROUP_PHYLUM,
    SUPERGROUP_PHYLUM == "Unannotated eukaryote" ~ "Eukaryote-Unannotated",
    TRUE ~ str_split_i(SUPERGROUP_PHYLUM, "-", 1))) %>%
  ###
  mutate(SUPERGROUP_PHYLUM_2 = case_when(
    # Dinoflagellates
    (SUPERGROUP_PHYLUM == "Alveolata-Dinophyta" & (is.na(Class) | is.na(Order) | grepl("SG_", Order))) ~ "Dinophyta-Unannotated",
    SUPERGROUP_PHYLUM == "Alveolata-Dinophyta" ~ paste("Dinophyta-", Order, sep = ""),
    # Ciliates
    (SUPERGROUP_PHYLUM == "Alveolata-Ciliophora" & (is.na(Class) | is.na(Order) | grepl("SG_", Order))) ~ "Ciliophora-Unannotated",
    SUPERGROUP_PHYLUM == "Alveolata-Ciliophora" ~ paste("Ciliophora-", Class, sep = ""),
    # Myzozoa
    (SUPERGROUP_PHYLUM == "Alveolata-Myzozoa" & (is.na(Class) | is.na(Order) | grepl("SG_", Order))) ~ "Myzozoa-Unannotated",
    SUPERGROUP_PHYLUM == "Alveolata-Myzozoa" & Phylum %in% myzozoa ~ paste("Myzozoa-", Phylum, sep = "")
    )) %>% 
  mutate(SUPERGROUP_PHYLUM_CLASS = case_when(
    SUPERGROUP_PHYLUM == "Alveolata-Ciliophora" ~ SUPERGROUP_PHYLUM_2,
    SUPERGROUP_PHYLUM == "Alveolata-Myzozoa" ~ SUPERGROUP_PHYLUM_2,
    SUPERGROUP_PHYLUM == "Alveolata-Dinophyta" ~ SUPERGROUP_PHYLUM_2,
    TRUE ~ SUPERGROUP_PHYLUM
  ))

# View(long_frenemies_annot_tax %>%
       # filter(grepl("Hacrobia", SUPERGROUP_PHYLUM)))

# sort(unique(long_frenemies_annot_tax$SUPERGROUP_PHYLUM))
# sort(unique(long_frenemies_annot_tax$SUPERGROUP_PHYLUM_CLASS))
# sort(unique(long_frenemies_annot_tax$SUPERGROUP_PHYLUM_2))
# unique((filter(long_frenemies_annot_tax, Supergroup == "Alveolata"))$SUPERGROUP_PHYLUM)
```

# Taxonomy resolution ladder  (grain)

For questions like _Is there a decoupling in taxonomy and functional trends across taxonomic levels?_, we need to evaluate if taxonomic and functional trends are consistent across different taxonomic levels/resolution/grain-levels. The goal is to determine how the taxonomy curve maps against the KO
function reference.
When we select a taxonomic resolution that is "cherry-picked", we run the risk of have a less appropriate output. If the story changes when we change the taxonomic level, that can be alarming and not responsible. Ramond et al. (2025) looked at how decoupling is only credible if it survives across grain, not at one cherry-picked resolution.

## Set up

Reload the handoff through `load_long_annot()` so the ladder sees exactly the table every later script sees (replicate-aware `sample_id`, `sample_unit`, `n_reps`).

```{r ladder-load}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
long <- load_long_annot()
```

### Build paired df

Shared prep for 02–06 (`R/prep_paired.R`): Gorda Ridge, Von Damm and Piccard; no per-row TPM cutoff; multi-KO transcripts split with TPM divided equally; Eukaryota-only and Opisthokonta lineages dropped. `depth = NULL` because the ladder assigns its own depth at each step.

```{r paired-table}
paired <- prep_paired(long, depth = NULL)
# head(paired)
meta <- paired |>
  distinct(sample_id, sample_unit, field, vent_bin, n_reps) |>
  arrange(sample_id)

# length((long$SEQ_ID)); length((paired$SEQ_ID))
length(unique(long$SEQ_ID)); length(unique(paired$SEQ_ID))
```


### Set up the grain ladder 

Write a function to go through each taxonomic level. 

```{r ladder-setup}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
# Same transcripts at every depth: keep rows with a resolvable lineage, rm NAs
paired_lin <- paired |> 
  filter(!is.na(full_classification))

# Grain ladder runs on the curated taxonomy (02 manual curation; 2026-10-12)
# depth 2 = curated supergroup, 3 = curated phylum (Syndiniales split from
# Dinophyta), 4 = class-level taxon inside its curated phylum, 5+ = deeper real
# ranks. See R/taxonomy_curated.R.
cur_key <- paired_lin |>
  distinct(full_classification, SUPERGROUP_0, SUPERGROUP_PHYLUM)
tax_at_depth <- function(d) {
  cur_key |>
    mutate(.tax = curated_lineage(full_classification, SUPERGROUP_0, SUPERGROUP_PHYLUM, d)) |>
    select(full_classification, .tax)
}

# deepest curated depth present
max_depth <- max(stringr::str_count(tax_at_depth(99L)$.tax, ";") + 1L)
# max_depth
```


```{r grain-fit-fn}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
# dat - input taxonomy matrix
# feat - input functional matrix
# label - add a label for matrix used
# Label grain - for the taxonomic level used. 
grain_fit <- function(dat, feat, label_matrix, label_grain) {
  tryCatch( # stop if error
    { # Build matrix for adonis2 fxn to run.
    bm <- build_matrix(dat, feat, min_tpm = 0, transform = params$transform)
    m  <- meta[match(labels(bm$dist), meta$sample_id), ]
    # PERMANOVA function
    perm <- run_permanova(bm$dist, m,
                          permutations = params$permutations,
                          seed = params$seed) |>
      filter(.data$term %in% c("vent_bin", "field")) |>
      select(term, R2, p)
    # dispersion check following permanova
    disp <- c(vent_bin = betadisper_check(bm$dist, m$vent_bin)$dispersion_p,
              field    = betadisper_check(bm$dist, m$field)$dispersion_p)
    #
    perm |> mutate(matrix = label_matrix, 
                   grain = label_grain,
                   n_features = ncol(bm$mat), 
                   dispersion_p = disp[.data$term],
                   skip_reason = NA_character_,
                   .before = 1)}, 
    error = function(e) {
    # if fails, stop.
    message(label_matrix, " grain ", 
            label_grain, " skipped: ", 
            conditionMessage(e))
    tibble::tibble(matrix = label_matrix, 
                   grain = label_grain, term = NA_character_,
                   R2 = NA_real_, p = NA_real_, 
                   n_features = NA_integer_,
                   dispersion_p = NA_real_, 
                   skip_reason = conditionMessage(e))
    })
}
```

```{r ladder-check}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
glimpse(paired_lin) # paired rows with a lineage (same as paired)
glimpse(max_depth) # Determined ceiling for taxonomic grain.
```

Start with taxonomy "2". taxa level 1 was only "Eukaryota" so it would have thrown an error. Note that these checks across taxonomic lienages also need to be run with all functional counts and then all with prevalence filtered data.
```{r ladder-run}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
# unfiltered and prevalence-filtered
## Across the different levels, 2 to the max_depth, run this function. Where we do a grain fit 
tax_curve <- purrr::map_dfr(2:max_depth, function(d) {
  dd <- paired_lin |> 
    left_join(tax_at_depth(d), by = "full_classification")
  bind_rows(
    grain_fit(dd,".tax", "taxonomy", d),
    grain_fit(prevalence_filter(dd, ".tax", 4), ".tax", "taxonomy_prev", d)
  )
})

# KO function reference (same two filters), horizontal line on the plot
fxn_curve <- bind_rows(
  grain_fit(paired_lin, "ko_id", "function", NA_integer_),
  grain_fit(prevalence_filter(paired_lin, "ko_id", 4), "ko_id", "function_prev", NA_integer_)
)
# _prev will be added to the prevalence filtered matrices.
```

```{r ladder-peek}
head(tax_curve)
head(fxn_curve) # Grain is NA, just the 4 options. 
```

View results.
```{r ladder-table}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
grain_curve <- bind_rows(tax_curve, fxn_curve)

readr::write_csv(grain_curve, "output-tables/02_grain_curve.csv")

grain_curve |> 
  arrange(term, matrix, grain)
```

### Annotation resolution by grain

Fraction of expression (scaledTPM) whose deepest retained rank is a real taxon name rather than a placeholder. Using TPM, not distance matrices, so it is independent of the rclr/distance choice. 

```{r resolution-by-depth}
# RM taxa with these:
placeholder <- "Indeterminate|Unannotated|incertae|_X$|^SG_|^Eukaryote$"

resolution_by_depth <- paired_lin |>
  mutate(n_real = stringr::str_count(lineage_depth(full_classification, 99L), ";") + 1L) |>
  expand_grid(grain = 2:max_depth) |>
  summarise(
    resolved_frac_tpm = sum(scaledTPM[n_real >= grain], na.rm = TRUE) / sum(scaledTPM),
    .by = grain) |>
  left_join(
    purrr::map_dfr(2:max_depth, \(d) tibble::tibble(
      grain = d,
      n_features = n_distinct(tax_at_depth(d)$.tax))),
    by = "grain")

resolution_by_depth

readr::write_csv(resolution_by_depth, "output-tables/02_resolution_by_depth.csv")
```

#### Supp figure S2
```{r grain-plot}
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-width: 13
ref <- fxn_curve |> dplyr::select(term, matrix, R2)   # KO reference lines

pal <- c(taxonomy = "#5a82b3", taxonomy_prev = "#34454c",
         `function` = "#eeb480", function_prev = "#c16b27")

p_grain_r2 <- ggplot(tax_curve, aes(grain, R2, color = matrix)) +
  geom_hline(data = ref, aes(yintercept = R2, color = matrix), linetype = 2) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = p < 0.05, fill = dispersion_p >= 0.05), size = 3) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 21, `FALSE` = 24),
                     name = "PERMANOVA p < 0.05") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "black", `FALSE` = "white"),
                    name = "Dispersion homogeneous\n(PERMDISP p >= 0.05)") +
  scale_color_manual(values = pal, name = NULL) + # USed Wada random 4-color
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:max_depth) +
  facet_wrap(~ term) +
  labs(x = "taxonomic depth (ranks kept)",
       y = expression(R^2~"(marginal)")) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "right",
        strip.background = element_blank())
```


```{r grain-plot-3}
# Plot the share of scaledTPM that resolves for each taxonomic depth.
frac_at <- function(g) {
  v <- resolution_by_depth$resolved_frac_tpm[resolution_by_depth$grain == g]
  if (length(v) == 1) round(100 * v) else NA_integer_
}

p_grain_tpm <- ggplot(resolution_by_depth, aes(grain, resolved_frac_tpm)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#34454c", width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::percent(resolved_frac_tpm, accuracy = 1)),
            vjust = -0.6, size = 3.2) +
  geom_text(aes(y = 0, label = paste0(n_features, " taxa")),
            vjust = 1.8, size = 2.7, colour = "grey35") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#34454c", `FALSE` = "grey82"),
                    guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:max_depth) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                     limits = c(0, 1.14), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = "taxonomic depth (ranks kept)",
       y = "scaledTPM classified to this depth") +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9),
        plot.margin = margin(5.5, 5.5, 14, 5.5))
```


```{r grain-plot-panel}
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-width: 13
(p_grain_r2 | p_grain_tpm) +
  patchwork::plot_layout(widths = c(2, 1)) +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(
    title = "Taxonomic grain: the answer is flat across grain, the coverage is not",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Left: marginal R\u00b2 per term. Dashed = KO function reference; ",
      "circles = PERMANOVA p < 0.05, triangles = n.s.; filled = homogeneous dispersion.\n",
      "Right: share of scaledTPM resolving to each depth (taxon count below each bar); ",
      "rank 4 highlighted."))

# ggsave("figures/tax-level-study-supp.svg", width = 13, height = 5, device = "svg", limitsize = FALSE)
```

Circles = PERMANOVA p < 0.05; triangles = n.s. Filled = homogeneous dispersion (PERMDISP p >= 0.05), so R² reads as a composition difference; open = groups also differ in spread (Anderson & Walsh 2013).

# Save the shared paired table

05, 05b, 06 and 07 all start from the same table: `prep_paired()` at the grain chosen above (rank 4) for Gorda Ridge, Von Damm and Piccard. Build it once here and save it to `data/processed/paired_L4.RData`, so those scripts load a small file (`load_paired()`, `R/load_paired.R`) instead of re-reading the ~420 MB handoff. The chunk rebuilds the file only when it is missing or older than the handoff or the prep code.

```{r save-paired}
#| message: true
PAIRED_FIELDS <- c("Gorda Ridge", "Von Damm", "Piccard")
PAIRED_DEPTH  <- 4L   # grain fixed by the ladder above

if (WRITE_HANDOFF || paired_is_stale()) {
  paired_L4 <- prep_paired(long, fields = PAIRED_FIELDS, depth = PAIRED_DEPTH)
  save_paired(paired_L4, fields = PAIRED_FIELDS, depth = PAIRED_DEPTH)
  rm(paired_L4); invisible(gc())
} else {
  message("paired_L4.RData is up to date; not rebuilt.")
}
```
